procedures: Read the skills:create reference format before authoring
Draft or refine the skill artifact in standard format (frontmatter + ## Input + ## Procedure)
Produce a sibling eval-pack JSON at paths.etcEvalPacks/<slug>.json
Optionally invoke scripts/etc/consult.js for a cross-provider critique
Verify the produced files against the standard format and schema

rubric.criteria: Skill follows the skills:create standard format: frontmatter description, ## Input, ## Procedure with at least 3 named steps
Paths are referenced as paths.X keys, not as bare literals; paths.etcEvalPacks is mentioned explicitly
The --consult path is documented and wired to scripts/etc/consult.js; flagged content is discarded
The skill documents producing an eval-pack with rubric, examples, and counterexamples
Is the skill well-organized, unambiguous, and consistent with the rest of the /etc namespace?

examples.input: /etc:author 'Create a skill that backs up the events log nightly'
expected_properties: Produces an eval-pack JSON at paths.etcEvalPacks/<slug>.json
Paths referenced as paths.X keys throughout
No root namespace .md file created alongside a subcommand directory

counterexamples.input: A skill file that hardcodes .claude/project/etc/eval-packs instead of paths.etcEvalPacks
must_not: creates a root .md alongside a subcommand directory
hardcodes absolute path literals where paths.X keys exist
invents a new authoring format instead of using skills:create
counterexamples.why: Violates the paths.X rule, the no-root-md subcommand convention, and the anti-goal of NOT inventing new authoring formats
